pr_body:
pci_get_hotplug_slot() has the following limitations:
- if slots are not hotpluggable, they are not in /sys/bus/pci/slots.
- the address at /sys/bus/pci/slots/X/addr doesn't contains the function part, so on some system, 2 different slots with different _SUN end up with the same hotplug_slot, leading to naming conflicts.
- it tries all parent devices until it finds a slot number, which is incorrect, and what led to NAMING_BRIDGE_MULTIFUNCTION_SLOT being disabled.

The use of PCI hotplug to find the slot (ACPI _SUN) was introduced in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/0035597a30d120f70df2dd7da3d6128fb8ba6051
"udev: net_id - export PCI hotplug slot names" on 2012/11/26.
At the same time on the kernel side we got https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/bb74ac23b10820d8722c3e1f4add9ef59e703f63
"ACPI: create _SUN sysfs file" on 2012/11/16.

Using PCI hotplug was the only way at the time, but now 12 years later we can use firmware_node/sun sysfs file.

Looking at a small selection of server HW, for HPE (Gen10 DL325), the _SUN is attached to the NIC device, whereas for Dell (R640/R6515/R6615) and Cisco (UCSC-C220-M5SX), the _SUN is on the first parent pcieport.

We still fallback to pci_get_hotplug_slot() to handle the s390 case and maybe some other coner cases (_SUN on grand parent device that is not a  bridge ?).

~Note: no idea if it works with s390, @niklas88 does `firmware_node/sun` exists for s390 ?~

Fixes #33598
pr_comments: (side note: I guess the SUN file was added in kernel 3.8. Our lowest baseline is 3.15, hence it's very much safe to use this file.)
@poettering @msekletar if you know anyone with s390 HW can you ping them (to check if sun exists or not and has a reasonable value)
@champtar I've pinged some contact at Red Hat about testing on s390. I will let you know if he gets back to me.
Is the `firmware_node/sun` some ACPI specific thing and when is it expected to exist? If it is for ACPI, then also other platforms like `ppc64le` are potentially affected as well.

On second look, this code [here](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/83c298547230039782c7ddc29446925dd268dfe4/src/udev/udev-builtin-net_id.c#L693) looks to me like it would fallback to the existing mechanism is the `fw_node/sun` is missing and I misunderstood the comments? So since s390 should never have this file I think it should be fine but would like to have my understanding confirmed.

@niklas88 no worries. I really don't know anything about s390 and didn't took the time to look in kernel source if it use ACPI ..., as you say it does not use ACPI, it'll fall back to the hotplug slot code and nothing will change.

Initially I wanted to get rid of the fallback for ACPI platform, but on second though if we keep some more names stable that's a win.

> Is the `firmware_node/sun` some ACPI specific thing and when is it expected to exist?

My understanding is that if ACPI _SUN is defined for a slot, you should have `firmware_node/sun` for the slot or the device in the slot. For ACPI platform, `/sys/bus/pci/slots/` already use ACPI _SUN, so we are just getting the information directly.

> If it is for ACPI, then also other platforms like `ppc64le` are potentially affected as well.

This will indeed impact all platform that use ACPI, not just x86_64

For anyone interested, here some udev rules to implement similar behavior (only works if `ID_NET_NAME_SLOT` is present, so you might want to go back to a naming scheme with `NAMING_BRIDGE_MULTIFUNCTION_SLOT` enabled):
```
cat > /etc/udev/rules.d/79-net-name-fixup.rules <<'EOF'
# https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/33682#issuecomment-2243225007
ACTION=="remove", GOTO="net_name_fixup_end"
SUBSYSTEM!="net", GOTO="net_name_fixup_end"

# no slot name or not an ethernet interface
ENV{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}!="ens*", GOTO="net_name_fixup_end"

# Get the ACPI _SUN from the NIC (HPE DL325gen10Plusv2 OCP NIC)
SUBSYSTEMS=="pci", \
  ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_SUN}="%s{firmware_node/sun}", ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_ADDR}="%b"

# Else get the ACPI _SUN of the first pcieport parent (Dell)
SUBSYSTEMS=="pci", DRIVERS=="pcieport", ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_SUN}=="", \
  ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_SUN}="%s{firmware_node/sun}", ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_ADDR}="%b"

# No slot info
ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_SUN}=="", \
  ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_NAME_BEFORE}="$env{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}", \
  ENV{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}="", \
  RUN+="/bin/logger 'NIC naming issue: _SUN not found, forcing path naming ($env{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT} -> $env{ID_NET_NAME_PATH})'", \
  GOTO="net_name_fixup_end"

# Generate new name as needed
PROGRAM="/bin/bash -c 'shopt -s extglob; i=$env{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}; s=$env{ID_NET_FIXUP_SUN}; [[ $$i =~ ens$$s[^0-9]* ]] || echo ens$$s$${i##ens+([0-9])}'"

# Naming mismatch, fixing
RESULT!="", \
  ENV{ID_NET_FIXUP_NAME_BEFORE}="$env{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}", \
  ENV{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT}="$result", \
  RUN+="/bin/logger 'NIC naming issue: slot mismatch, renaming ($env{ID_NET_FIXUP_NAME_BEFORE} -> $env{ID_NET_NAME_SLOT})'"

LABEL="net_name_fixup_end"
EOF
```

It needs to also be present in the initramfs

issue_context.title: udev: Use parent pcieport firmware_node/sun for slot number
issue_context.body:
EDIT: acpi_index -> firmware_node/sun

### Component

systemd-udevd

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Having interface name match physical slot name makes sysadmin life simpler.

In `NAMING_BRIDGE_MULTIFUNCTION_SLOT` we tried to get the slot information from
```
# ls /sys/bus/pci/slots
1  3
# cat /sys/bus/pci/slots/1/address
0000:80:03
```
As the slot address is missing the function it can (and does) conflict in some case.

At least Dell R6615 / R7615 with PCI riser it conflicts (pcieport are .1 and .2), but the NIC parent is a pcieport with `firmware_node/sun`, so it might be a safe way to retrieve the slot number.

Some commands on a system with udev naming scheme = v252 (ie with `NAMING_BRIDGE_MULTIFUNCTION_SLOT`)
```
# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/uevent
DRIVER=pcieport
PCI_CLASS=60400
PCI_ID=1022:14A5
PCI_SUBSYS_ID=1028:0AF6
PCI_SLOT_NAME=0000:80:03.1
MODALIAS=pci:v00001022d000014A5sv00001028sd00000AF6bc06sc04i00
# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/firmware_node/sun
1
# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/label
SLOT 1
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/0000:81:00.0/net
ens1f0
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/0000:81:00.1/net
eth1
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/0000:81:00.2/net
ens1f2
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/0000:81:00.3/net
ens1f3

# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/uevent
DRIVER=pcieport
PCI_CLASS=60400
PCI_ID=1022:14A5
PCI_SUBSYS_ID=1028:0AF6
PCI_SLOT_NAME=0000:80:03.2
MODALIAS=pci:v00001022d000014A5sv00001028sd00000AF6bc06sc04i00
# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/firmware_node/sun
2
# cat /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/label
SLOT 2
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/0000:82:00.0/net
eth4
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/0000:82:00.1/net
ens1f1
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/0000:82:00.2/net
eth6
# ls /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/0000:82:00.3/net
eth7
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

If NIC direct parent is a pcieport AND has `firmware_node/sun`, use it as slot number

### Describe alternatives you've considered

do nothing and keep using pci path naming

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

256
comments:
> Having interface name match physical slot name makes sysadmin life simpler.

Your suggestion directly contradicts it.

Your example shows a system with physical slots 1 and 3. This is a valid configuration for e.g. for PowerEdge R6615 you mention. Next you suggest assigning slot `#2` based on some obscure `_DSM` returned value. How exactly having device in slot `#2` makes sysadmin life easier if this slot does not really exist? How sysadmin is expected to match this device to physical slots present in the server?

It sounds more like a kernel issue. The `/sys/bus/pci/slots/N/address` is generated by kernel which cuts out the function number. If physical topology wires different functions to different physical slots, may be kernel needs to show it?

Slot 2 definitely exists for the sysadmin or the smart hands in the datacenter, it doesn't exists only for udev.

here a screenshot from iDRAC (Dell OOBM)
![image](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/assets/3536755/9ad5960d-848e-4cdb-a5e8-17aee6709f8f)

and a picture from Dell website
![server-poweredge-r6615-black-gallery-10](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/assets/3536755/17090367-f1e7-4187-ad73-a32720841b93)

`/sys/bus/pci/slots` seems to be for hotplug slots, and according to the iDRAC screenshot the slots are not hotpluggable (not sure how to check via sysfs)

Dell R6615 have multiple riser cards possible, so the slots might or might not exists (https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-ca/oth-r6615/r6615_ism/expansion-card-installation-guidelines?guid=guid-3a81bb8a-afdf-4d33-b7b6-28b19c542836&lang=en-us)

The obscure `_DSM` value as you call it is actually the value people want.

`/sys/bus/pci/slots` seems like an indirect / fallback way to get the info, and adding the function to `address` would be a breaking change.
Looking at the parent acpi_index seems straight forward but maybe I'm missing something.

>  Looking at the parent acpi_index seems straight forward but maybe I'm missing something.

Actually looking at a Dell R640, I see
interface = ens2f0np0
acpi_index = 18
label = SLOT 2

so `acpi_index` is indeed a bad idea

Maybe we can parse the `label` for some basic pattern ?

> `acpi_index = 18`

Yes, you were just lucky that on another system this value happened to match physical slot number.

> Maybe we can parse the `label` for some basic pattern ?

If you can provide a link to or at least quotation from the official standard that defines `label` content - yes, it could be possible. But to my best knowledge it is absolutely arbitrary string.
```
bor@bor-Latitude-E5450:~$ cat /sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:19.0/label
 Onboard LAN
bor@bor-Latitude-E5450:~$ 
```
Still, no `label` for another, wireless, interface.

I went and did some digging, the use of PCI hotplug to find the slot (ACPI `_SUN`) was introduced by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/0035597a30d120f70df2dd7da3d6128fb8ba6051 on 2012/11/26.
The commit lakes description, but at the same time on the kernel side we got https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/bb74ac23b10820d8722c3e1f4add9ef59e703f63 on 2012/11/16, so I guess PCI hotplug, even if indirect and imprecise (cuts the function part) was the only way at the time.
We are now ~12 years later so we can likely rewrite `pci_get_hotplug_slot_from_address` and just read `/sys/bus/pci/devices/ADDRESS/firmware_node/sun`, that would fix the issue with Dell R6615/R7615.

This would not fix the issue with Dell R740xd2. If we look back at https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/28929, we have NIC/pcieport/pcieport/"pcieport with label". I think we could have a NAMING_BRIDGE_MULTIFUNCTION_SLOT_V2 that stop at the first parent pcieport, so we get back slot naming for a lot of hardware.

> that would fix the issue with Dell R6615/R7615

It is rather difficult to guess without any real information. Tell the server model number, the exact riser configuration, in which (riser) slots the network cards are installed and interface names of them and properties from at least two interfaces in (presumably) different slots:
```
udevadm info --attribute-walk /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/0000:81:00.0/net/ens1f0
udevadm info --attribute-walk /sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/0000:82:00.1/net/ens1f1
```
or whatever names those interfaces got.

> stop at the first parent pcieport, so we get back slot naming for a lot of hardware.

The issue you mention has full attribute listing for one interface. Explain which attribute(s) of which parent node could be used to assign slot number.

R6615, with (looking at only docs and matching with iDRAC) a R2A riser, with NICs in slot 1 and 2
This 2 issues are:
- missing hotplug slots
`# ls /sys/bus/pci/slots`
`1  3`

- possible slot confusion as those pcieport have function number != 0
`/sys/bus/pci/slots/1/address: '0000:80:03'`

Using `firmware_node/sun` fixes both issues
```
/sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/label: 'SLOT 1'
/sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.1/firmware_node/sun: '1'
/sys/devices/pci0000:80/0000:80:03.2/label: 'SLOT 2'
```

if the "firmware_node/sun" file doesn't exist, shouldn't we fall back to the old ways?
